stem: P, Q, R, S, T, U, V each visit on a different day Mon-Sun. Q visits Wednesday. P visits just before S. T visits after Q but before V. U visits Sunday. Who visits Monday?
solution: With Q Wed and U Sun, P-S adjacent pair and T between Q and V constrain the grid; R is forced to Monday.

stem: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing north. C sits middle. A sits next to C on the left. E sits at an end. Who sits at the other end?
solution: C=3, A=2, E=1 or 5. B and D fill remaining seats; either can be at the free end, so undetermined.

stem: In a class, E scored 90 and ranked 3rd, F scored 84 and ranked 5th. If no ties between ranks 3-5, what did the 4th rank score?
solution: Rank 4 lies strictly between rank 3 (90) and rank 5 (84), so between 84 and 90.

stem: Four people live on floors 1-4. A lives above B. C lives just below D. B is not on floor 1. Who lives on floor 1?
solution: C just below D gives pairs (1,2),(2,3),(3,4). A above B with B not on 1 forces C on floor 1.

stem: P - Q means P is sister of Q, P ÷ R means P is daughter of R, R x S means R is brother of S, S + T means S is mother of T. In P - Q ÷ R x S + T, how is P related to T?
hint: R x S makes R uncle/aunt line.
solution: P is daughter of R; R is brother of S; S is mother of T. So P and T are cousins.

stem: Six boxes stacked 1 (bottom) to 6 (top). Box M is above K by two positions. J is just below M. L is at top. Which box is at bottom?
solution: L=6, J=M-1, M=K+2 gives valid stacks with different bottoms, so undetermined.

stem: Four teams split into two groups of two. A and B cannot be together. C must be with D. How many valid groupings?
solution: C-D fixed as a group; remaining A,B split so A-B apart is automatic within 2v2 structure; 2 ways to label groups.

stem: Find the odd one out: EKDG, KQJM, NTMP, OULQ.
solution: First three follow +6,-7,+3 pattern on positions; OULQ breaks it.

stem: If CAT = 24 and DOG = 26, what is BAT?

solution: Pages compose a book as bricks compose a wall.

stem: A city expanded bus lanes and bus ridership rose 20%. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Bus lanes caused all of the rise
Bus lanes likely contributed to the rise
solution: Correlation with a plausible mechanism supports 'likely contributed', not absolute causation.

stem: Argument: 'The new library will raise reading scores because students will borrow more books.' The argument assumes:
solution: The causal bridge is that borrowed books translate into higher scores.

stem: All managers passed the audit; some auditors are managers. Which follows?
solution: Auditors who are managers passed, so some auditors passed.

stem: Claim: nightalmente study lowers scores. Which most strengthens it?
options: A controlled trial shows lower retention after late nights
solution: A controlled trial directly supports the causal claim; anecdotes do not.
